notes:
Summary: mid-market B2B SaaS (customer onboarding/chat agent) evaluating Redwood hosted first, plans Dedicated if POC meets latency and cost targets. Primary focus: conversational assistant that uses tool calling (calendar, billing lookup) and streamed progressive responses to improve perceived latency. Key asks from security team: SSO/SAML integration, SOC2 evidence, ability to redact/obfuscate PII from operational logs (not just in-model masking), retention controls (30/90/365 day options), and KMS for encryption of customer data.

POC requirements / success criteria (from VP Product / Eng):
- Start-of-stream first-token latency: p95 <= 300ms on hosted region-na with streaming enabled.
- End-to-tool-call roundtrip (tool invocation + model response): p95 <= 800ms for common flows.
- Support for streaming partial tokens and server-side function/tool calling hooks (must support synchronous tool call pattern).
- Logging: redact email/SSN/credit-card patterns before storing traces; provide an out-of-the-box redaction pipeline or a documented webhook to receive raw events for customer-side processing.
- Audit: provide access logs, per-request routing info, and retention TTL controls.
- Cost: bound per-conversation cost predictably; interested in batching/kv-cache recommendations to lower unit cost.

Security notes from the security review call: "We need SSO/SAML configured via Okta and SCIM for user provisioning — show us a working integration." Also: "SOC2 Type II report or timeline to obtain it; we can start on hosted with compensating controls but need roadmap." Legal asks for data residency statement for EU customers (they have EMEA customers, likely later). Engineering also asked about fallback policies (auto-fallback to smaller model variant on congestion), metrics for per-route latency breakdown, and observability hooks to correlate tokens <-> trace ids.

Open items: pricing for Dedicated slot + burst; SLA for hosted latency (what can be promised for p95 streaming); formal PII redaction implementation (where in pipeline, who owns it), and whether hosted logs can be configured TTL per-customer. Next scheduled: start hosted POC 2026-03-08 (2 weeks), provide Redwood with sample request traces and a set of 200 eval prompts reflecting heavy tool usage.
